memory_update.text: High-fit direct candidates for government procurement/compliance modernization include PLTR, BAH, LDOS, PANW, and OKTA.

The strongest chokepoint markers in this node are FedRAMP High authorization, DoD IL4/IL5 eligibility, ATO history, IDIQ/GSA contract access, cleared workforces, agency incumbency, and funded backlog.

Additional candidates to evaluate in later passes: CACI, SAIC, ManTech if publicly accessible after ownership changes, Accenture, IBM, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Zscaler, CrowdStrike, Fortinet, Tyler Technologies, Thomson Reuters, Parsons, and Maximus.

This pass did not fully map USAspending obligations, SAM.gov award IDs, FedRAMP Marketplace product-by-product status, or agency-level recompete calendars; those are required for Layer 2 evidence scoring.
PLTR is a high-confidence direct software candidate for government AI/data modernization because FedRAMP High and DoD IL6 authorizations map tightly to the node’s certification bottleneck.

BAH and CACI represent the systems-integrator/cleared-workforce side of the node; their bottleneck is procurement access, cleared talent, cyber expertise, and agency incumbency rather than a single scarce physical component.
ZS and OKTA are targeted cyber/identity software candidates where FedRAMP High authorization supports public-sector relevance, but materiality to consolidated revenue still needs verification.

The highest-value evidence for this node is not generic federal exposure; it is authorization status, IDIQ/GSA contract-vehicle access, DoD impact-level clearance, agency ATO reuse, recompete history, and backlog/obligation data.

Need a follow-up pass on FedRAMP 3PAOs, CMMC assessors, GSA/SAM procurement data vendors, secure cloud hosting providers, and niche vulnerability/exposure-management vendors such as Tenable or Qualys.
CACI added as a high-confidence Alliant 3 federal IT modernization and cybersecurity contract-vehicle candidate for the government procurement/compliance node.
SAIC added as a federal systems integrator with Alliant 3 exposure; watch for task-order evidence rather than relying only on vehicle eligibility.
Telos added as a below-$1B exception due to direct Xacta exposure to FedRAMP/RMF authorization and compliance workflows.
Okta added as a public-sector identity candidate with FedRAMP High authorization; federal revenue materiality needs verification.
Zscaler added as a zero-trust/CMMC/FedRAMP adjacent cybersecurity candidate; public-sector contribution and DIB demand need quantification.

For this node, procurement access and compliance authorizations appear as important as product quality: Alliant 3, FedRAMP High, DoD IL4/IL5, CMMC alignment, and authorization-workflow tooling are the key mapping variables.

Need a follow-up pass on private but strategically important channel partners and aggregators such as Carahsoft, Guidehouse, Persona, and other FedRAMP-authorized identity/compliance vendors because they may explain demand flow to listed suppliers.

The highest-fit names for this pass are government-native data/software platforms, federal systems integrators with cleared workforces and contract vehicles, cybersecurity vendors with FedRAMP High authorization, and identity platforms positioned for zero-trust mandates. This is research-support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded universe for government-facing compliance and modernization chokepoints. The strongest candidates are not generic politics plays; they map to hard-to-replicate authorization, procurement, cleared-workforce, cyber, identity, and agency-incumbency constraints. This is research universe expansion only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded universe for the government procurement/compliance/digital modernization node. The strongest underappreciated mapping is not simply defense primes, but companies with pre-competed federal IT contract vehicles, FedRAMP High or DoD IL authorizations, identity/zero-trust roles, or compliance automation tools that shorten agency authorization and procurement cycles.
